title: LLM-Assisted Causal Discovery: Mapping Hidden Patterns in Crystalline Solids
content: The discovery of novel materials relies on developing causal models to explain property emergence. While classical approaches rely on physical principles and experiments, the growing volume of observational data necessitates learning causal relationships from data. We integrate high-resolution STEM data with domain-specific insights from fine-tuned LLMs [1] (e.g., ChatGPT trained on ferroelectrics literature) to construct Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) [2] mapping causal links between structural, chemical, and polarization features in Sm-doped BiFeO3 (SmBFO). This approach helps hypothesize how synthesis conditions influence material properties, guiding experimental validation. Ultimately, we aim to unify LLM-driven literature analysis with data-driven discovery for precise ferroelectric material engineering. To infer causal relationships among key descriptors of SmBFO without prior domain knowledge, we employed the PC (Peter-Clark) [3] algorithm using Gradient-Based Causal Structure Learning (gCastle) [4]. This process began with skeleton identification, where all variables were initially interconnected. Conditional independence tests were then applied iteratively to remove statistically insignificant connections. For instance, if Px​ (In_plane_polarization) and a (Lattice_parameter) were found to be conditionally independent given I14 (Intensity of A-cation columns (Bi, Sm))​, their direct link was eliminated, forming the refined skeleton graph. Next, we oriented the remaining edges by identifying v-structures (e.g., I14→a←Volume) and applying deterministic rules to direct causal chains (e.g., I14→a→Volume). This process resulted in a DAG, representing potential causal pathways, allowing us to analyze variable interdependencies and directional influences in the SmBFO system.
